comparison: Both evaluate pantoate binding structural evidence (C4, C54, C62-C69) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes crystallographic quality (2.3 Å resolution) and ITC validation. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'convincing' and 'solid and rigorous.' OpenEval covers broader claim set including stability assays (C48-C53, C56) not explicitly mentioned in peer evaluation.

Partial overlap on binding evidence (C48-C52). OpenEval R1 evaluates these as part of comprehensive structural validation. Peer R2 focuses specifically on binding assays and thermostability, describing them as 'convincing' and 'solid.' Both SUPPORTED, but peer review separates binding assays from structural characterization.

Both evaluate structural comparisons showing conformational changes (C11-C12, C71-C75, C80, C134) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative displacement measurements and control structure validation. Peer reviewer notes 'modest movements...consistent with providing coordination of the substrate.' High agreement on structural observations.

Perfect claim overlap (C9-C10, C87-C93, C95) with identical SUPPORTED evaluation. Both affirm MD simulation findings on sodium's role in pantoate stability. OpenEval details simulation parameters (0.5 μs, three replicates). Peer reviewers describe simulations as 'convincing' with 'intriguing insights' and note 'marked reduction in RMSD' with sodium present.

Perfect claim overlap (C81-C84, C98) with identical SUPPORTED evaluation. Both affirm mutagenesis data on pantoate binding. OpenEval notes unexpected T112 mutation results and entropy-driven binding. Peer reviewers describe binding assays as 'convincing' and studies as 'solid and rigorous' without questioning the findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C85-C86) with identical SUPPORTED evaluation. Both affirm structure-activity relationship data showing pantoate specificity and importance of hydroxy-acetate group. OpenEval references Figure 5 supplement data. Peer reviewer confirms analog studies 'demonstrate the specificity of pantoate as a substrate.'

Partial overlap on TM1 movement observations (C58-C61). OpenEval evaluates broader claim set (C57-C61, C77-C79) as SUPPORTED with quantitative RMSD values. Peer R5 focuses on TM1 opening substrate site to cytosol (C58-C61, C76, C104-C105), also SUPPORTED. Both accept TM1 structural findings without challenge.

Both address elevator mechanism compatibility (C109-C112) but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on structural modeling consistency. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting mechanistic proposals 'would be better supported by transport data' and Reviewer 4 highlighting that 'all crystal structures belong to the same conformational state.' Peer R7 also includes unlocking mechanism claims (C114-C117, C136) that OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Significant overlap on unlocking mechanism (C114-C117, C136). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation lacking experimental validation. Peer review also UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating proposals 'would be better supported by transport data.' Both identify these mechanistic interpretations as requiring further validation, showing strong concordance on limitations.

Perfect claim overlap (C118-C123) on extrapolation to plant BASS transporters. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculation requiring experimental testing. Peer review rates SUPPORTED without explicit challenge, accepting sequence conservation arguments and broader implications. Divergence in evaluation stringency for extrapolative claims.

Substantial overlap on human transporter extrapolations (C124-C128, C140). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculative mechanistic extrapolation despite cited mutagenesis data. Peer review also UNCERTAIN, noting the field 'remains uncertain about bile acid binding' and proposals are 'presented as speculation.' Both recognize limitations in extending findings to mammalian transporters. Peer R10 also includes C129-C132, C139 addressed in OpenEval R11 and R20.

OpenEval R11 addresses NTCP structure analysis (C129-C132) rated UNCERTAIN as explicitly speculative. Peer R10 includes these claims in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of human transporter mechanisms, acknowledging ongoing uncertainty about bile acid binding modes. Both recognize speculative nature of these proposals.

Minimal overlap (C94 only). OpenEval R12 evaluates biological relevance claims (C94, C45-C47) as SUPPORTED based on sequence analysis and literature. Peer R2 includes C94 in binding data evaluation, also SUPPORTED. Both affirm pantoate as biologically relevant substrate.

OpenEval evaluates sodium's mechanistic role (C96-C99, C137-C138) as UNCERTAIN, noting explicit speculation despite MD support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific mechanistic proposals about sodium structuring the binding site.

Minimal overlap (C100-C101 on binding site location). OpenEval R14 evaluates binding site characterization and conservation (C100-C108) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C100-C101 in structural findings evaluation, also SUPPORTED. Both affirm binding site identification in crossover region.

Minimal overlap (C104-C105 on TM1 role). OpenEval R14 includes these in broader conservation analysis rated SUPPORTED but notes TM1 role inference is speculative. Peer R5 includes these in TM1 movement evaluation, also SUPPORTED. Both accept structural observations.

OpenEval evaluates background structural features of BASS transporters (C23-C27) as SUPPORTED based on established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent contextual background rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.
